analysis.answer: Under current law, a person 21 or older who can lawfully possess a handgun may carry it concealed without a permit. The measure changes this by prohibiting permitless concealed carry and requiring individuals to obtain a permit from the county sheriff.
The measure adds a new requirement that applicants must complete an eight-hour safety course to obtain the required concealed carry permit.
Direct costs include the fee for the eight-hour safety course, plus the opportunity cost of the time spent attending it. Local governments face administrative costs to process and issue the permits.

Individuals who wish to carry a concealed handgun bear the costs of the safety course and the time required to complete it. County sheriffs bear the administrative burden of processing applications. The public may benefit from improved firearm handling and safety among those carrying concealed weapons.
Firearm instructors will likely see increased demand for safety courses. Some handgun owners may choose not to carry concealed due to the new time and cost requirements.

The measure addresses the potential public safety risk of untrained individuals carrying concealed handguns by mandating safety training. However, this mechanism creates a new barrier to entry for individuals wishing to carry a concealed weapon.
Firearm instructors and businesses offering safety courses gain a mandated customer base. County sheriffs gain the administrative role of issuing the permits.
Administrative resources will be required for county sheriffs to intake applications, verify background eligibility and course completion, and issue the physical permits.

flags.quote: The sheriff shall issue a permit
flags.note: Mandates that county sheriffs issue permits but does not provide funding or authorize an application fee to cover the administrative costs of the program.
Does not specify who is qualified to teach the course or what content it must cover.
